title: Four-try hero as Jillaroos survive almighty World Cup wake-up call... and sight sparks ‘concern’
text:
Women’s Rugby League World Cup 2026: Jillaroos survive big scare against Fiji, Jaime Chapman injury update, final against New Zealand date HOME NRL WORLD-CUP Four-try hero as Jillaroos survive almighty World Cup wake-up call... and post-game sight sparks ‘concern’
 Church sends Aussies to the final | 00:31 Martin Gabor from Newswire November 8th, 2026 8:51 pm The Jillaroos have set up a trans-Tasman World Cup final showdown but only after they survived an almighty scare from Fiji who have unearthed a future NRLW star.

 Australia trailed early but kicked clear to win 30-14 in their closest game of the tournament a week after they scored a world record 124 points against Wales.
 They were sloppy in the first half and were rattled by Fiji’s physicality before they finally clicked into gear with winger Abbi Church delivering a Sunday sermon with four tries. 
 She got the Aussies on the board in the 24th minute as the back three combined for all six tries.
 Tamika Upton and Jaime Chapman both crossed the line, but this was Church’s time to shine as she completed her hat-trick before she put the icing on top with a stunning 78-metre kick return as the sun set on Fiji’s World Cup.
 The Jillaroos will be raging favourites to beat the Kiwi Ferns in Sunday’s final given they smashed them by 50 in the World Cup decider four years ago.
 But this has to be a wake-up call for them because New Zealand will bring the physicality through the middle and have the talent in the spine to score points.
 Elsewhere, Chapman failed to finish the game after what was described as cramping, but was pictured post-game with ice on her hamstring.
 “There might be some slight concerns for Jaime Chapman. It was reported that there was some cramp, but we didn’t witness any cramping,” Corey Parker said on Channel 7.
 Chapman told Channel 7’s Jelissa Apps it was “precuationary” and she would be “all good” for the final.
 Jaime Chapman after the game. Source: FOX SPORTS 
 WHAT A START 
 The Washington Generals would have been given more of a chance of beating the Harlem Globetrotters than Fiji had of knocking over the Jillaroos.
 But the upset of the century was on the cards right up until half-time as Fiji threw the form book out the window.
 They took it to Australia from the opening whistle with a number of Jillaroos stars whacked as the tournament favourites coughed up the ball eight times in the first half.
 It allowed Fiji to dominate field position which saw Talei Holmes held up over the line before the underdogs opened the scoring via a penalty goal.
 Allianz Stadium was then stunned after 15 minutes when five-eighth Luisa Yaranamua caught the defence napping from dummy-half to make it 8-0.
 Yaranamua must be on the radar of NRLW sides after she peppered the back three with towering bombs and set up Fiji’s second try with a glorious cut-out pass.
 She was the second best player on the field, but Fiji just lacked the attacking class to turn half chances into points as the Aussies kicked away late.
